findings.summary: crates/athena-core/src/code_health.rs is not among the reading's deliverables
findings.evidence: A change outside the listed deliverables widens the scope.

findings.summary: Shared test helpers are classed as production callers
findings.evidence: code_health.rs:75-80: is_cfg_test matches only the exact meta `cfg(test)`. crates/athena-core/src/lib.rs:164-165 declares `#[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-support"))] pub mod test_support;`. Its file crates/athena-core/src/test_support.rs, and every file in crates/athena-testkit/src/, pass is_measured (a /src/ path not named tests or *_tests). Their calls would be shown as production sites, ahead of real test sites. Fix: Also count as test a path under crates/athena-testkit/ and crates/athena-core/src/test_support.rs, or treat a `cfg(any(test, ..))` attribute as test in the scan's own check. Leave code_health's measure unchanged. Alternatively, have the label say that test-support helpers may appear as production.
findings.location: Step 4, site classification `test = !is_measured(path) || in_test`; Decision 2 (is_cfg_test shared)

findings.summary: Common names such as `new`, `run` and `path` sort first and can push core-flow functions past the cap of 30
findings.evidence: The index is keyed by bare name, so every `X::new(..)` and `.run(..)` in the workspace counts toward a deliverable's `new` or `run`. Sorting by `elsewhere` descending puts those names first. run/mod.rs declares about 60 functions (fn lines from mod.rs:198 to 2669, as the plan says), so the real callers of functions like produce_and_verify (mod.rs:1872) may fall into '(+N more)'. Fix: Sort by the number of distinct production files with a call site, or, for an ExprCall with a qualified path (`Type::name`), count it only when the qualifier matches the deliverable's impl self type or the file's module. Keep the approximate label either way.

findings.summary: The critic is not given the computed caller list, so it cannot compare a plan's dependents against it
findings.evidence: The plan leaves critic_brief unchanged (CriticInputs has no deliverable facts, planner.rs:177). The introspection 20261116-003943-6ch3 that the reading cites proposed a rule 'checked by the critic and by code where possible'. No acceptance criterion requires this, so it is not a gap in the criteria. Fix: Optional: say in the CHANGELOG limits that the critic does not see the computed list, or propose passing the same CallerList to the critic as follow-up work.

summary: Round 2. Both round-1 majors are resolved. (1) Test code is marked per item by a syn visitor, not by cutting the file at a column-0 #[cfg(test)], and the fixture has a production fn after a mid-file `#[cfg(test)] mod seam {}` (`after_the_seam`). (2) The scan uses syn, which is already a dependency (crates/athena-core/Cargo.toml:23; Cargo.toml:51; span-locations at Cargo.toml:49), and shares code_health's is_cfg_test and is_test_fn (code_health.rs:75, :82). The round-1 minors (cat_blobs at lib.rs:988, caps on all three lines, citing tests.rs:10876) are also addressed. I checked the plan's claims in the snapshot: the loop at planning.rs:121-129 is the only production constructor of DeliverableFact, and planner_brief( is called only at planning.rs:147. The Report format string (planner.rs:170) and the size-bound test (briefs.rs:4164-4179) are as described. The fixtures (repo, commit_file, planning_script, prompts_of, finished_job) exist. is_measured (code_health.rs:195) classes the separate-file test modules (run/tests.rs, gh/after_merge_tests.rs, run_pin_tests.rs, landing_tests.rs) as test code. The dependents list matches the readers I found. Each demonstration calls a real entry point (planner_brief; Athena::deliverable_facts over a real temp git repo) and would fail without the change. I found three minor issues and no blocker or major, so the verdict is accept.
